newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sees avge 97 inflation meeting target.
newsitem.headline: Italy sees avge 97 inflation meeting target.

text.p: Italian inflation continues to fall satisfactorily and a government target of an average 1997 rate of 2.5 percent appears to be within reach, according to a summary presented to parliament on Friday of official quarterly state accounts.
Separately, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told a news briefing that a 1998 average inflation target of 2.0 percent, also set by the government, was "more than credible".
Inflation in Italy has fallen steadily in the past year to its lowest levels since 1969.
Economists said earlier that they forecast March inflation of 0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.2 percent year-on-year against 0.1 and 2.4 percent in February.

They made their forecasts after 11 sample cities completed publication of their preliminary consumer price index data. Final March CPI data will be released by national statistics institute on April 7.
